author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan will acquire an AI-powered satellite imagery system capable of rapidly identifying People’s Liberation Army ships, aircraft and missile launchers, as it seeks to boost early-warning capabilities in the face of growing military pressure from Beijing.
The NT$46.55 million (US$1.45 million) system will use artificial intelligence (AI) to analyse satellite images covering 100 sq km (38.6 square miles) within minutes, potentially cutting the time and manpower needed to track changes in PLA...
title: How Taiwan’s new AI satellite system aims to speed up early warning against PLA moves

author: Shi Huang
description:
China’s embassy in Thailand has warned citizens to carefully plan their trips and pay extra attention to transport security following a string of high-profile kidnappings targeting Chinese nationals.
Online influencers and artists were also advised to remain vigilant against high-paying job scams operating in Thailand in the latest such warning issued on Friday.
There have been a number of high-profile incidents in recent months in which online celebrities and travellers were kidnapped in...
title: China’s embassy issues fresh Thailand travel alert over kidnappings, job scams

author: Carol Yang
description:
Donald Trump was apparently captivated by the “beautiful” roses in the garden of the Communist Party’s leadership compound when he visited Beijing in May.
It was a relaxed moment between the US and Chinese leaders – otherwise locked in disputes ranging from trade to technology and Taiwan – that led to a new opportunity for gift diplomacy between the rival powers.
Strolling around the former imperial garden at Zhongnanhai with Xi Jinping, Trump was so taken with a China rose variety in bloom that...
title: Coming up roses? How Trump planted a new seed for Chinese gift diplomacy

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
There is “no way out” for corrupt officials no matter how senior they are, China’s top anti-corruption watchdog has warned following the downfall of a former big-city mayor who survived numerous previous scandals.
This week, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) announced both the probe into Huang Qifan, the former mayor of Chongqing, and the expulsion of a senior figure in Sichuan province.
On Saturday, the commission said these developments showed the party’s “unwavering...
title: Corrupt officials have nowhere to hide, China’s anti-graft watchdog warns

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
In Shenzhen, drones are banned, shiny new hotels have opened their doors and taxi drivers are carrying devices that can translate nearly 150 languages.
Since President Xi Jinping announced last year that China’s southern tech hub would host Apec meetings in November, the city has done all it can to get ready under the watchful eyes of the local, provincial and national authorities.
While every Apec summit draws the world’s attention, this year’s edition is considered to be especially high-stakes...
title: Is China’s Shenzhen ready to host Xi, Trump and Putin during Apec summit?

author: Shi Huang
description:
For patients with advanced, metastatic cancer that has progressed despite systemic therapy – options remain critically limited.
Now, Chinese scientists are pointing to an unconventional therapeutic agent – the element iron.
This idea originated in industrial waste water treatment: iron can react with hydrogen peroxide to generate hydroxyl radicals, which degrade various organic and toxic molecules in waste water.
Chinese scientists wanted to treat malignant tumours the way they treat waste water...
title: Landmark China trial gets 84% efficacy in treating cancer with cue from waste water tech

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
The owner of a Chinese kindergarten has been jailed for life after more than 200 children were poisoned by lead in the country’s worst food safety scandal for almost two decades.
A total of six people were jailed on Friday for making or selling harmful foodstuffs by Lanzhou Intermediate People’s Court in Gansu province.
Li Huifang, owner of the Peixin Kindergarten in Tianshui, was handed a life sentence and fined 500,000 yuan (US$75,000), while Zhu Jinglin, the principal, was jailed for 15 years...
title: Chinese kindergarten owner given life sentence over lead paint poisoning scandal

author: Richard Heydarian
description:
China and the Philippines recently traded accusations over the medical evacuation of a Philippine serviceman from a grounded naval vessel in the hotly disputed Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea. The incident has sparked renewed worries about potential armed skirmishes in a global artery of trade.
But Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr was also quick to emphasise the economic dimensions of a major conflict. After a decade of rapid economic growth, the Philippines is facing...
title: Philippines’ ‘China-free’ manufacturing strategy is a high-risk bet

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Beijing’s decision to allow a bigger Japanese business delegation to go to China next month may be cause for some optimism but “hot economics and cold politics” will continue to dominate the strained relationship between the two countries, observers say.
Kyodo news agency reported this week that Beijing had agreed to allow the Japanese Business Federation – the country’s most influential business lobby, also known as Keidanren – to expand its delegation coming to China next month.
The group will...
title: ‘Hot economics, cold politics’: why China gave nod for expanded Japanese trade trip
